features.feature_value: Removes when posts are primarily insulting/name-calling; prefers many viewpoints but not blatant disrespect.
features.evidence_span: it was because it was more about insulting and name calling
features.rationale: The participant explicitly ties their (limited) removals to insulting/name-calling rather than politics content.

features.feature_value: Kept/remade decisions by considering both versions together, anchored in respect for both parties.
features.evidence_span: I decided to make the decisions as a pair
features.rationale: They describe their strategy as making decisions for the pair while applying a respect-based standard.

features.feature_value: Language that attacks/uses inappropriate terms influences their judgment to remove/keep.
features.evidence_span: Inappropriate language and attacking individuals influence my vote.
features.rationale: Their stated decision driver is inappropriate language and attacking individuals.

features.feature_value: Uses a First Amendment framing; since no direct threats to individuals, posts are acceptable.
features.evidence_span: None of these posts had direct threats toward a single individual, so they are fine
features.rationale: They specify a concrete threshold (no direct threats) under a general free-speech principle.

features.feature_value: Leans toward allowing speech even if it’s inflammatory, citing the 1st amendment and only blocking the truly inflammatory/bad.
features.evidence_span: I erred on teh side of allowing it since we have the 1st amendment
features.rationale: They explicitly state their tendency and rationale for allowing over removing.

features.feature_value: Draws a line at insulting opposite views via emotional/ad hominem rhetoric not backed by facts (intended to provoke rage).
features.evidence_span: insulting people of opposite views with emotional/hysterical ad hominem language
features.rationale: They describe a specific content pattern (ad hominem, emotionally manipulative framing) as the removal criterion.

features.feature_value: Visualizes posts as if seen online and chooses those that don’t seem appropriate to remove.
features.evidence_span: I imagined seeing the posts online and chose the ones that didnt seem appropriate to remove.
features.rationale: Their method is about imagined online impact/appropriateness, not comparing ideology between pair versions.

features.feature_value: Confused by agreeing with one but not the other; sees it as making no sense.
features.evidence_span: I did not like that I agreed with one but not the other I thought this does not make any sense
features.rationale: Their reflection centers on discomfort/confusion about inconsistent judgments across the pair.
